review_kind: Luna scalar capability and byte type source review
source_basis: Vendored docs/instcombine/source plus pinned external /tmp/instcombine-Instructions.cpp and /tmp/instcombine-PatternMatch.h; Puddle verifier/interpreter and Byte.Basic sources.
scope: Read-only inventory capability review. No Lean, inventory, manifest, or status changes.

source_evidence.text: if (!GEPEltType->isIntegerTy(8) && GEP.hasAllConstantIndices())
if (GEP.accumulateConstantOffset(DL, Offset))
Comment: Canonicalize constant GEPs to i8 type; branch replaces the GEP with Builder.CreatePtrAdd(...)
restricted one-dynamic-index GEP is scaled by DataLayout.getTypeAllocSize; default layout is RV64

findings.finding: The source action applies to non-i8 source element type with all-constant indices and an accumulable offset. IRBuilder::CreatePtrAdd constructs a GEP with i8 element type; it does not introduce a separate LLVM opcode. A source refinement limited to an unflagged, one-index i64 constant GEP under default RV64 is within the documented GEP interpreter scope, subject to proof. The inventory rewrite opcode getelementptr is correct.
findings.recommendation: Keep the restored modeled specialization pending proof and retain blockers for flags, arbitrary layouts/index widths, and wider GEP shapes.

source_evidence.text: foldCmpSelectOfConstants is the caller that computes a four-entry truth table and synthesizes a Boolean expression with createLogicFromTable.
ICmp visitor calls foldCmpSelectOfConstants.
FCmp visitor calls foldCmpSelectOfConstants.
createLogicFromTable is the shared formula constructor used by that helper.

findings.finding: L8701 is the shared foldCmpSelectOfConstants action, reached from both integer and floating comparison visitors; createLogicFromTable at L3143 builds its result. It is not an FCmp-only rule. Its constant arms are compared by CmpInst truth table and the result is composed from constants, existing select conditions, NOT, AND, OR or XOR.
findings.recommendation: Keep scalar flag-free integer comparison/select specialization pending. Keep FCmp, vector, and samesign behavior explicitly outside the modeled subset.

source_evidence.text: match(NotOp, m_OneUse(m_BitCast(m_Value(X)))) and match X as one-use Cmp
m_Not is m_c_Xor(m_AllOnes(), V)
cst_pred_ty specializes matching constants to ConstantInt
Non-pointer BitCast is valid when source and destination primitive bit widths are identical.

findings.finding: The pinned source branch has no distinct-type guard. A scalar `icmp` result bitcast i1-to-i1 is a legal no-op bitcast and Puddle models that integer bitcast, so the degenerate scalar shape is genuinely admitted by source matching. However, m_Not requires an all-ones ConstantInt, so this is an integer NOT shape; it does not introduce ByteType NOT semantics.
findings.recommendation: Retain the scalar-i1 specialization as pending proof. Keep vector/FCmp exclusions. Do not generalize this row to ByteType merely from bitcast support.

source_evidence.text: inttoptr normalizes source width only when it differs from pointer size
ptrtoint normalizes result width only when it differs from pointer size
inttoptr interpreter accepts only 64-bit integer source.
ptrtoint interpreter accepts only 64-bit integer result.

findings.finding: Under default RV64, the 64-bit source/result forms accepted by Puddle do not satisfy the LLVM rewrite guard. The nontrivial widths that trigger the rewrite are not interpreted, so unsupported classification is correct for these entries.
findings.recommendation: Keep the guard-scoped unsupported status; do not claim the identity-width case as implementing this normalization.

source_evidence.text: Trunc castIsValid requires source and destination isIntOrIntVectorTy.
Non-pointer BitCast is valid when primitive bit widths are identical.
Pointer bitcasts are limited to pointer/byte combinations; pointer-pointer casts require matching address spaces.
InstCombine replaces byte constants with integer constants in stores using a bitcast.

findings.finding: LLVM ByteType is distinct from IntegerType. It admits same-width bitcasts to/from integer and pointer/byte bitcasts; LLVM CastInst::castIsValid rejects ByteType for trunc/zext/sext because those casts require isIntOrIntVectorTy. Pointer-pointer bitcast chains are valid only for matching address spaces.
findings.recommendation: Treat same-width integer<->byte bitcast composition as a source candidate for cast-L243. Treat ptr->ptr->ptr same-address-space bitcast composition as a distinct modeled candidate; it preserves the pointer value through no-op casts and needs no memory reconstruction. Consider source compositions P->P->B, P->B->B, and P->B->I as additional candidates only where each exact cast-pair and intermediate type is valid. Any Byte->pointer intermediate must be reviewed for whether ptrFromInt can return none for some memory state, which could make an interpretation proof vacuous.

source_evidence.text: LLVM.Byte defines per-bit poison and/or/xor operations.
and/or/xor verifier dispatches to verifyIntegerBinop (checkIsNonNullIntegerType only checks integer width/signedness).
verifyIntegerBinop requires both operands to pass verifyIntegerType.
Interpreter and/or/xor cases destructure .int operands; there is no .byte branch.
Shift verifier accepts integer-or-byte data operand and integer shift amount.
shl has an explicit .byte interpreter branch.
lshr has an explicit .byte interpreter branch.
trunc verifier calls verifyTruncTypes with allowByte=true.
verifyTruncTypes accepts byteType-to-byteType when allowByte=true and widths shrink.
trunc interpreter has a .byte branch.
LLVM source castIsValid nevertheless excludes ByteType trunc.
freeze interpreter accepts .byte.
bitcast interpreter includes byte conversions.

findings.finding: Byte.Basic defines pure Byte.and/or/xor functions, but current LLVM OpInfo does not expose those as well-formed interpreted operations: and/or/xor dispatches to verifyIntegerBinop, which requires integer operands, and their interpreter cases accept only `.int`. Byte shifts are verifier-valid and interpreted. Byte trunc is also verifier-valid in Puddle (`allowByte=true`) and its interpreter has a `.byte` branch; LLVM CastInst::castIsValid still rejects it, so it creates no LLVM source ByteType variant. Freeze and bitcast have actual Byte runtime branches. checkIsNonNullIntegerType itself only constrains integer width/signedness and does not reject ByteType.
findings.recommendation: For LLVM inventory classification, count ByteType only where source type legality and Puddle verifier/interpreter both support the required operations: principally freeze, bitcast, shl/lshr. Do not infer source Byte trunc variants from Puddle support, or infer operational byte and/or/xor from helper definitions.

source_evidence.text: commonCastTransforms delegates cast-pair composition to Instruction::isEliminableCastPair.
Cast-pair case 18 allows bitcast-bitcast to bitcast for non-pointer endpoints or same-AS pointer endpoints.
Case 18 separately describes pointer->byte->integer and integer->byte->pointer compositions.
Same-width non-pointer bitcasts are valid.
Integer-to-integer equal-width bitcast preserves value.
Integer-to-byte equal-width bitcast maps the integer bits into Byte.
Byte-to-integer equal-width bitcast is interpreted.
Pointer-to-pointer bitcast preserves the pointer RuntimeValue.

findings.finding: The source bitcast/bitcast pair table admits candidate semantic subsets beyond integer cast chains: same-width scalar integer↔ByteType compositions; same-address-space pointer→pointer→pointer compositions; and table-specific pointer/byte/integer endpoint forms (including P→P→B, P→B→B, and P→B→I where legal widths/types line up). Puddle interprets integer/byte bitcasts and same-AS ptr→ptr without memory reconstruction. Pointer/byte conversion uses address conversion; Byte→pointer reconstruction calls ptrFromInt and must be checked for state-dependent failure before claiming a non-vacuous semantic proof.
findings.recommendation: Add/retain precise pending variants for same-width integer/byte composition and same-AS pointer-only composition under cast-L243. Record P→P→B, P→B→B, and P→B→I as candidates requiring exact cast-pair/path checks; scrutinize every Byte→pointer intermediate for ptrFromInt totality over modeled memory states. Do not claim byte truncation or broad pointer-byte composition.

source_evidence.text: m_Not is typed as XOR with cst_pred_ty<is_all_ones>.
cst_pred_ty specializes the constant matcher to ConstantInt.
m_Not returns m_c_Xor(m_AllOnes(), V).

findings.finding: The NOT-related bitwise inventory families (including bitwise-L1758, L2114/L2121/L2136/L2175/L2183, L5187/L5244, L5277/L5291, and L5363/L5370/L5380) cannot be broadened to ByteType based on generic formulas: m_Not requires a ConstantInt all-ones value, while ByteType is a distinct constant/type family. The outer and/or/xor operations also lack Byte verifier/interpreter support in Puddle.
findings.recommendation: Keep these entries integer scoped unless a particular source pattern proves a separate legal ByteType form.

findings.finding: Many scalar bitcast inventory rows include select, compare, arithmetic, or trunc operations; Puddle's select interpreter accepts integer arms only, comparisons are integer-only, and trunc is not Byte-valid. A Byte bitcast at one point in a source pattern is insufficient to make the whole rewrite a modeled Byte specialization.
findings.recommendation: For future broad byte audit, trace every required matched and emitted opcode through LLVM cast/type legality, Puddle verifier, and interpreter; source BitCast eligibility alone does not confer end-to-end support.

summary: The three restorations are source-supported: GEP CreatePtrAdd emits the canonical i8-element GEP, cmpb-L8701 is shared by ICmp/FCmp, and bitwise-L5370 includes the scalar i1 no-op bitcast shape. cast-L2740/L2820 remain unsupported because only width-mismatched forms trigger their source guards. Byte source/interpreter scope is operation-specific: byte bitcast/freeze/shl/lshr are modeled; and/or/xor are not verifier-valid in Puddle; byte trunc is verifier-valid/interpreted by Puddle but LLVM CastInst::castIsValid excludes it. cast-L243 additionally has same-width int/byte and same-address-space pointer-only composition candidates; pointer/byte round trips require care around ptrFromInt partiality.
